Attach physical attributes to a scale

Source: R/attributes.R
attach_attributes_scale.Rd

This feature may change or be removed in a later version.

Appends rows to the object's attribute table. A row names the member it belongs to (frame, member), the attribute (attribute, e.g. "lhv"), its kind (see SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS), its value, an optional lower/upper range, the physical unit_of_measure ("GJ/t", "kg/TJ"), the source the figure was taken from and an optional note. Values can be attached at any frame: a calorific value for a whole carrier is inherited by every fuel under it that has no value of its own (see scale_attributes()).

Usage

attach_attributes_scale(x, attributes, source = NULL, kind = NULL)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

attributes

A data.frame with columns frame, member, attribute, value, unit_of_measure, and optionally lower, upper, note; kind and source as columns or through the arguments.

source

Optional single string filled into the source column when attributes has none.

kind

Optional single string filled into the kind column when attributes has none.

Value

The scale with the rows appended.

Details

Existing rows are never overwritten: a row whose (frame, member, attribute, source) already exists is an error. Attach a second source under its own source name and choose between them with source= when reading.

Examples

s <- scale_example()
s2 <- attach_attributes_scale(
  s,
  data.frame(frame = "class", member = c("G1", "G2", "S1"),
             attribute = "density", value = c(10, 20, 5),
             unit_of_measure = "t/m3"),
  source = "survey", kind = "property"
)
scale_attributes(s2, "density", frame = "item")
#>   frame member attribute     kind value lower upper unit_of_measure source note
#> 1  item     U1   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 2  item     U2   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 3  item     U3   density property    20    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 4  item     U4   density property    20    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 5  item     U5   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 6  item     U6   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 7  item    OTH   density     <NA>    NA    NA    NA            <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#>   origin_frame origin_member
#> 1        class            G1
#> 2        class            G1
#> 3        class            G2
#> 4        class            G2
#> 5        class            S1
#> 6        class            S1
#> 7         <NA>          <NA>
